title: Biorthogonal-only Floquet Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: Jiangrong Wen, Qidong Yuan, Zi-Xiang Hu, Jian-Jun Dong
abstract: Non-Hermitian dynamical quantum phase transitions (DQPTs) are intrinsically sensitive to the choice of inner product under nonunitary time evolution. Although the biorthogonal formulation based on associated states provides a normalized Loschmidt echo with a probabilistic interpretation, previous studies have found biorthogonal and self-normal DQPTs to occur in the same parameter regimes, suggesting that the two forms of dynamical criticality are concomitant. Here we demonstrate that this is not the case. In an exactly solvable periodically driven non-Hermitian Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain, we uncover a finite biorthogonal-only Floquet DQPT regime, where the biorthogonal Loschmidt rate becomes nonanalytic while the self-normal Loschmidt rate remains smooth. The critical conditions are obtained analytically, showing that the onset of biorthogonal Floquet DQPTs is locked to the exceptional lines of the effective Floquet Hamiltonian, whereas self-normal criticality has no corresponding spectral boundary. Moreover, for each critical momentum, the biorthogonal DQPT exhibits a pair of critical times within every driving period, whereas the self-normal DQPT exhibits only one. Our results establish a fundamental distinction between biorthogonal and self-normal DQPTs, thereby opening a route toward new nonequilibrium quantum phenomena in non-Hermitian systems.
summary: The paper investigates Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions (DQPTs) in a driven non-Hermitian SSH chain by comparing two mathematical formulations: biorthogonal and self-normal. The key finding is that these two approaches are not equivalent, revealing a regime where only the biorthogonal method predicts a transition. This establishes a crucial theoretical distinction for understanding non-equilibrium physics in open quantum systems.
main_problem: To fundamentally distinguish between Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions (DQPTs) identified using biorthogonal versus self-normal inner products in non-Hermitian systems.
main_result: The authors demonstrate a finite regime where only the biorthogonal formulation predicts a DQPT, showing that the choice of overlap structure dictates the existence of dynamical criticality. This establishes a fundamental distinction between the two types of transitions.
method: Theoretical analysis using the Loschmidt echo formalism applied to a periodically driven non-Hermitian SSH chain, comparing the rates derived from biorthogonal and self-normal inner products.
model_or_system: The study uses an exactly solvable, periodically driven non-Hermitian Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain model. The dynamics are analyzed via its effective Floquet Hamiltonian in momentum space.
key_observables: Biorthogonal and self-normal Loschmidt echo rates ($\lambda_B(t)$ and $\lambda_S(t)$), which exhibit nonanalyticities signaling a DQPT.
important_parameters: Dimerization ($\eta$) and intracell nonreciprocity ($\gamma$), which define the parameter space for the transition regimes.
main_assumptions: The analysis is performed on an exactly solvable model (SSH chain) using specific time-evolution parameters ($\hbar=1, \omega=2$).
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically shows spectral regimes separated by exceptional lines in the parameter space $(\eta, \gamma)$. Figure 3 illustrates the comparison of $\lambda_B(t)$ and $\lambda_S(t)$ across different spectral conditions.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the problem of DQPTs in non-Hermitian systems. It then develops the mathematical framework using both biorthogonal and self-normal Loschmidt echoes for the SSH chain. The core is the comparison, leading to the identification of the Biorthogonal-only regime and a discussion of the differing temporal structures of critical times.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses non-equilibrium quantum dynamics in open/non-Hermitian systems, which are highly relevant for understanding dissipation, gain, and topological properties in modern AMO platforms like photonics or superconducting circuits.

figures.caption: Figure 1. (a) Schematic of the periodically driven non-Hermitian SSH chain, with the dashed box indicates a unit cell. (b) Four spec- tral regimes of HF (k) in the (η, γ) parameter plane, separated by exceptional lines corresponding to kc = 0 and kc = π. Region I is real-part gapless at both kc = 0 and kc = π; Regions II and III are real-part gapless only at kc = 0 and kc = π, respectively; Region IV exhibits a ﬁnite real-part energy gap across the entire Brillouin zone.

Figure 2. (a) Real parts of the dispersions Re Ek,± in Regions I– IV. (b) Corresponding biorthogonal Loschmidt rates λB(t). Circles mark the critical points. The parameters are (η, γ) = (0.85, 4.75), (2.5, 6), (0.2, 2.5), and (2.0, 2.0) for Regions I–IV, respectively.

Figure 4. Global Floquet-DQPT diagram for the biorthogonal and self-normal formulations in the (η, γ) plane. The four regimes, B- only, Both, S-only, and None, indicate whether a Floquet DQPT oc- curs only in the biorthogonal formulation, in both formulations, only in the self-normal formulation, or in neither formulation, respec- tively. The black dashed curves mark the exceptional lines, which coincide with the onset boundaries of biorthogonal Floquet DQPTs. The purple solid curves mark the self-normal DQPT boundaries de- termined by Eq. (14).

Figure 3. Representative comparisons of the biorthogonal and self- normal Loschmidt rates for the same Hamiltonian parameters, initial state, and time evolution. Circles mark the corresponding critical points. (a) Biorthogonal-only: λB(t) develops nonanalytic cusps, whereas λS(t) remains smooth. (b) Both: both rates exhibit nonana- lyticities. (c) Self-normal-only: nonanalyticities occur only in λS(t). (d) Neither: both rates remain analytic. The parameters (η, γ) are (0.5, 5.5), (−0.15, 2.6), (−1.5, 2.5), and (2.0, 4.4) for (a)–(d), re- spectively.
